title: Count by Grade
description: Write a query to count students in each grade.
solutionSql: SELECT grade, COUNT(*) as count FROM students GROUP BY grade;
explanation: GROUP BY groups rows with the same grade, and COUNT(*) counts each group.

title: Average Age by Grade
description: Write a query to calculate the average age of students in each grade.
solutionSql: SELECT grade, AVG(age) as avg_age FROM students GROUP BY grade;
explanation: GROUP BY creates groups, and AVG() calculates the mean for each group.

title: Count by Department
description: Write a query to count teachers in each department.
solutionSql: SELECT department, COUNT(*) as count FROM teachers GROUP BY department;
explanation: Each department forms a group, and COUNT(*) tallies teachers per department.

title: GROUP BY Purpose
description: What does the GROUP BY clause do?
explanation: GROUP BY groups rows that have the same values into summary rows.

title: HAVING Clause
description: Write a query to get grades that have more than 1 student enrolled.
solutionSql: SELECT grade, COUNT(*) as count FROM students GROUP BY grade HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
explanation: HAVING filters groups after aggregation, unlike WHERE which filters rows before grouping.

title: Predict Group Result
description: What will this query return? SELECT grade, COUNT(*) FROM students GROUP BY grade;
explanation: The query groups students by grade and counts each group.

title: Fix GROUP BY Error
description: This query has an error. Fix it: SELECT grade, name FROM students GROUP BY grade;
solutionSql: SELECT grade, COUNT(*) as count FROM students GROUP BY grade;
explanation: When using GROUP BY, all selected columns must either be in the GROUP BY clause or used in an aggregate function.
brokenQuery: SELECT grade, name FROM students GROUP BY grade;

title: Total Credits by Department
description: Write a query to get the total credit hours offered by each department.
solutionSql: SELECT t.department, SUM(c.credits) as total_credits FROM courses c JOIN teachers t ON c.teacher_id = t.id GROUP BY t.department;
explanation: JOIN connects courses with teachers, then GROUP BY department sums credits per department.
